Example: Instead of assigning priorities to tasks, things offers the possibility to drag tasks into the desired order e.g. according to importance.
I ask the developer to keep this simplicity because sometimes are less possibilities more!

But I’d like to propose some additional modifications:
1. Assign tasks to „evening“ should be possible for all days
2. Integrate the possibility to enter calendar events
3. Add the possibility to use different colors for tasks
4. Reminders should be possible for all future tasks on the desired date and time

title: Finally it has dark mode!
body:
It’s gorgeous, and it keeps getting better!

But I do have a bunch of recommendations.

- Needs a button for "tomorrow" in the calendar. At the end of a day, I like to organize my thoughts about what I should do the following day. So a tomorrow button would be incredibly helpful!
- Wrap long items to next line. The "..." doesn't help! This would greatly help me to quickly see what I need to finish for the day. 
- When a list of checklist items are exported from another app, they aren't imported as to-do items in Things. Import & exporting still need some improvements. 
- Projects should have colors to help distinguish them apart. That way, the different types of things that I need to finish each day are easier to identify. 
- Also, instead of pie charts, custom icons (like Ulysses) would be SWEET! Pie charts are funny, because where I need it most is for today, but that’s a star!
- Swiping on a heading shows a "Delete" option, but tapping on its "..." button shows a "Remove" option.
author: MasPollo

title: Great, but would love attachment support
body:
I think Things is amazing, but missing better attachment functions. I understand why they want to keep things simple, but I personally prefer to work out of a task management app (Things) and not my email. Right now, I can save the email to a folder on my Mac, make a task and link the email...this works, it’s just too many steps. I would even be happy to pay a monthly payment for it if it’s their storage that’s the problem (or if they can integrate iCloud, that would be even better). Anyway, exactly the same app, better email support and these features:
- forwarding of emails removes “Fwd:” from the task when it shows up. 
- add commands I can put in the email to schedule it, tag it, and put it where I want on the email forward, not just land in the inbox. For example, and email with the subject “Fwd: Help with Email!”, if I add this to the subject, it will automatically tag it, assign to a date, and drop in a project. The subject I forward is “Fwd: Help with Email! [12/19/18][tags: tag1, tag2][Project:ABC]”

This will make a task, with the entire email content (or even attach the email I’m forwarding), it will be scheduled to show up in “today” on 12/19/18, automatically tagged “tag1” and “tag2”, and be put into the project “ABC” if it exists, if not, either create it or just drop into the inbox (this can be the devs choice). 

Feel free to contact me for more info and this would easily make my rating go to a 5 stars and be the perfect task management App. I would even be willing to test it if interested. 

Thanks, and I hope to help make this a perfect task manager!!

body:

But there isn’t enough functional integration with calendar to make this useful for me. I can see my calendar items but can’t open them or do anything with them which leaves me to have to jump to another app to work with meeting invites and other calendar items. This is a fatal flaw with this app for me, sadly. 

I’ve been on Informant Pro for years since that app integrates calendar and tasks so well. But have been trying to find something else that is more elegant and simpler. I thought this was going to be it until I discovered how severely limited it is with respect to calendar. Oh well, the search continues, and another $10 down the drain.

Edit: I’ve come back again to Things 3 because it seems that I’ve become sort of hooked on how extraordinarily well it handles tasks. I’ve decided to try to live with using a separate calendar app along with Things and see how it goes. Hopefully in the future the authors will consider adding at least some ability to edit or even open calendar items in Things. Meanwhile I try this setup.

2. Complete

I suggest:
1. Complete
2. Snooze

This will more closely match Apple’s Reminders app, which organizes the action menu:
1. Complete 
2. Remind me in 1 Hour

title: Missing Important Feature
body:

When I use the repeat feature and select “daily” I should be presented with a Sunday to Saturday format that allows me to select the days of the week that I want this task to repeat. Say, for example, I want a task repeated every MWF, I would tap on M, W, and F individually, and that task would be added to every MWF in my calendar.

title: Great app, just one suggestion!
body:
This app is seriously life-changing. Being an adult with ADHD this really helps manage my tasks and to-dos. It takes a little time to get used to it, but once you do, it’s so easy to customize, move tasks around, change dates, etc. I love that I can get the same information on my MacBook and my iPhone so that I’m always on track. 

The one thing I have not seemed to find in any app is the ability to allocate specific timeframes for each task. With this app, you can easily see tasks you need to complete for “today”, but I would love to be able to designate times for each task and receive reminders when I should be moving on to the next task. With this one change, this app would really do everything!

body:

title: 😍 Only 1 Thing Missing
body:
I am smitten with this app. I used to get by with a paper planner, then switched to Todoist last year, but I hated that there was really no way to see upcoming tasks beyond a week. Things has solved that problem for me (and then some!) — no more worrying about an annual subscription, waaaay better integration with Apple Watch and my calendar (thank goodness), and a simpler, cleaner interface that allows me to organize everything from daily tasks to vacation ideas and workout plans. The price seemed a little steep at first, especially since it wasn’t easy to try out the app before I bought it, but it was worth every penny.

Now, the only thing I’m missing is a way to track daily habits. I end up with a ton of to dos every day, which is a pain, because I just want a separate part of the platform that allows me to track that stuff. I’ve tried Streaks but would really like to have all these features in one place.

author: NanMann

title: Great, With hopes for a few enhancements
body:
Overall, this app is great and has really helped me tame my to dos so far. As others have said, it’s the perfect harmony of elegance and power. And from my experience with other apps, the appearance of simplicity and ease is deceptively important otherwise I tend to start to ignore my to dos. 

There’s a few things I hope they add to bring this app to the next level:

- Allow to indicate particularly important to dos and have them show up at the top of Today so I can easily see them. 

- Allow to schedule checklist items within a to-do for different days, and make the checklist in general a bit less hidden within the overall app interface

- Add subfolders

- Offer a website-based version with lite functionality so that people who have apple products but do work on PCs (A.K.A. Engineers) can still access their todos via a computer during the day. 

Overall, this app is the best I have found for organization. With the addition of those features, the app would go from “great” to “perfect” for me.

title: Perfectly Intuitive.
body:
This app is essential to objective management without the worry of forgetfulness that sometimes hangs over our lesser priorities. The UI is simply shy of beautiful, but with updates seemingly a regular practice I foresee Things only getting better.

Cons:
 - No dark theme, unlike the desktop ver.
 - No option to add sounds/songs to reminders.

Anyway, good app and the cost, albeit a tad high, is worth it for those who like to have a stable manager of their life's objectives.
author: Jack B. Eanstalk

title: Great app with some downfalls
body: Let me start off by saying this is a fantastic task managing application. That being said, it is really only catered to iOS and MacOS. So if you use windows don’t expect any kind of web client. Furthermore there is also large pay walls to this application. You will have to purchase the iOS app, iPad app, and the macOS app. You’re looking at upwards of $30 spent on a task manager that is arguably missing key features that free task manager apps offer. For one it doesn’t have a dark mode, you can’t set task priority, no multiple reminders on tasks or reminders on sub tasks and the biggest one, no windows support. This is a great app but if you’re looking for an application that can handle multiple platforms without a hitch then i would look towards TickTick or Todoist.

author: Connie Han

title: Nearly perfect iOS app
body:
I used ToDo on the iPhone with Toodledo on the web for years, and I was quite happy with it. However when I tried to update ToDo, as it was increasingly buggy, to ToDo Cloud, the install failed and I started looking around. And I am glad I did. I looked at many reviews and decided to give Things 3 a try.

The tutorial is well done, and in 15 minutes I was fully up to speed. I then reentered about 100 tasks, although I could have imported them. I have to state that the interface is a joy to work with, and the final result was amazing. 

Read the reviews for product details, but this app defines what is great about iOS.  Clean, intuitive and fun. The integration with the calendar, in particular, is brilliant. 

After getting it set up on the iPhone, I purchased the iPad app.  Perfect integration and interface!

My only quibbles... When I set an Inbox item to Today, and then I do not complete the task and clear the date, the task ends up in the Anytime folder. I think it should go back to the Inbox.  This is by design, and I have a workaround, but it is mildly annoying. Also, I would like to not display the Anytime folder, as I do not need it, but this is not customizable. I could use the real estate for another area or project.  But these are minor details. This is one of the best apps for iOS. Period.

author: MrGlover

title: Scam! Deceptive description to squeeze more money out of you
body: This app was highlighted in one of the app store’s daily lists. It looked like the productivity app I’ve been looking/hoping for, but at $9.99, I was reluctant to jump in without even a trial version. I should have listened to that inner voice. I decided to go ahead and buy it, because if Apple is highlighting it, it’s probably worth the ten bucks, right? Wrong. To my unpleasant surprise, once paid for, downloaded, and opened on my iPad, I got a message saying this was the iPhone version (even though the App Store description says it supports iPhone AND iPad), and I could go to the App Store to get the iPad version. I headed to the App Store, but they wanted $19.99 for the iPad version—on top of the $9.99 I already paid for an app I can’t use (my phone is an Android, and not the platform I want to use for my productivity apps, anyway.) I’m sorry, but if you’ve already cheated me out of $10 by misrepresenting your product, I’m not going to give you another $20. I’ll be making a formal complaint to Apple.

title: Finally!
body: I first used Things years ago to GTD. After I discovered Wunderlist, I switched and loved the flexibility and the plethora of features it offered. Few years ago, a tragedy took place and Wunderlist fell victim to Microsoft who bought out and stopped updating the app. It then went off to attempt its own version of Wunderlist, only to release an underdeveloped, underperforming iteration that's probably doomed for the lack of user interest. To make a long story short, I was forced to find a replacement for my beloved Wunderlist (RIP). I searched high and low only to return to Things 3. I'm happy to acknowledge that it evolved into a prince, matching and at times surpassing Wunderlist. Things 3 is more elegant and user friendly then any other app I've tried. I'm happy to be home again. My dream is for Apple to recognize the value of Things 3 and purchase it. Only then can we be assured that this magnificent product will survive indefinitely. Apple, are you listening?!

title: Things 3 means more productivity
body: I’ve used this app for almost a week and so far I’m noticing that I’m more productive than ever. I like that it gives me my to-do list every morning. I can also set up specific reminders to make sure I get the essential things done. And I’ve been able to tackle mini projects through it. Even though it displays my calendar events, I wish it could also serve as a calendar such that I don’t need to go to my actual calendar to schedule appointments or events that aren’t projects or to-do’s. title: Great app, could use a few minor improvements
body:

Having read a book that explains the Getting Things Done (GTD) method, I decided to give Things another try (I had owned a previous version). 

The UI is streamlined easy to use, clean, and intuitive. 

Few improvements / suggestions:
I would be great to be able o add images, contact info, or other media in the notes section of each to-do. 

It would also be wonderful if the app was location aware so tasks could be tied to a specific location. 

Also, this app can get expensive given that there are 3 versions (iPhone, iPad, and MacOS). I understand the MacOS versión being a different product, but the mobile & tablet versions should be part of the same purchase. 

Overall, great product!

title: I’ve used every to-do app... blah blah blah
body:

I’ll summarize this app for you:

• Gorgeous and intuitive interface
• Flawless synchronizing between iOS and macOS
• Compatible with Priacta’s TRO workflow
• If you think it should do something, it probably does

I really didn’t think so much functionality could be put into an elegant, yet simplified interface. It doesn’t lack features, it just doesn’t overwhelm you with them when they aren’t needed.

Amazing job Cultured Code! This is my fourth product purchase from you. I have always been happy with them, even if the product is a little slower to market than I’d wish sometimes, it is always well worth the wait.

title: Incredible for daily use
body:
I was a long time Things user, but prior to Things 3, I felt like there were limitations that held it back, to the point where certain things were deal-breakers and I started looking elsewhere for task management. I’m glad to say, though, that not only has Things 3 been my go-to task manager since launch, it works so well that I don’t feel the siren call of other apps.

Everything is really inviting and thought out. Things supports to-dos, from simple tasks to involved projects, with deceptive simplicity. What really works for me is that there’s more of an emphasis on when a task should be accomplished, as opposed to where it is filed in the system. I feel like this works so well because it’s so easy to reschedule tasks. That’s not to say you can’t impose an organizational structure to your tasks - I use Areas extensively to file stuff for the Office, Home, Personal tasks, and so on - but flexibly scheduling stuff works so well for me. I never lose track of what I could be working on.

Cultured Code should also be commended for their rock-solid sync service. I’ve never had an issue keeping task state synced across iPhone, iPad, and Mac. It’s easy to set up then gets out of your way.

I have one small wish-list item, that I know I’ve seen other folks raise as a problem: I would love to complete future repeating tasks early. Right now, a repeating task will show up in Upcoming, but that’s only when the template will create another single instance of itself. It’s something I can work around - I set the repeat date to the first day that I could possibly want to start work on the task, and reschedule as needed - but it is a tiny bit of unnecessary friction in an otherwise smooth system.

That aside, fantastic app. Definitely worth your money!

title: Disappointing to a long time Things 2 user
body:
I’ve used Things 2 for many years and finally took the plunge and purchased Things 3 because of its ability to integrate with Calendars. 

I have to say- I’m very disappointed. 

Cons:
1. The Today view in Things 3 now looks like a big cluttered mess because To-Do’s in different areas aren’t divided off into different sections. You can’t even change the font color. So, things I need to do at work and things I need to do at home aren’t easily and quickly visually distinguishable when looking at my day. This is a big set back from Things 2.

2. There’s a nice new feature to move To-Dos to “This Evening.” But, after the end of the day, things that were scheduled for evening, move back to the same cluttered mess with all the other to-do’s. I’d really like to see an upgrade that allows scheduled recurring to dos to be created under the “this evening” heading. For example, I always go to the gym at night. I’d like that reminder to appear there rather than have to move it every day.   

Pros:
1. The calendar integration is very well done

It's a real pain to then create tasks in Things after the meeting by re-typing the action items into my phone. 

With a web app I could at least enter my tasks on the Surface while in the meeting. 80% of my tasks are work related, in a Windows Enterprise, while all my personal device's are all iOS/Mac. I'm stuck using Todoist until something better comes along with web support or Windows client.

title: Good app. Looking for a few things to be added
body:
I usually don’t pay this much for an app, but when I read articles looking for the best to do apps for ppl who just want the day to day todos up front, this was the one!  It is very streamlined and has almost everything I could want. I’ve used a lot of todo apps before and this is working the best so far. I love the ability to create projects and organize them by type. I created an event category and add each event that is coming up as a project. Things does the countdown for the events for me and that really helps. I like things a lot but I am begging for some additions. 

- color coding or icons - I am a visual person. I’d love to be able to color code things either based on tags or timelines or manually depending on my mood :) icons would be a nice plus too but color is the top. 

- I really wish I could open my things via a web browser on my PC. I don’t use Mac but with so much to do some days, being able to open it on my computer would be very helpful. 

- I wish I could see today and “upcoming” at the same time without the back and forth. I’m often looking at today and deciding if I can push something to tomorrow but in Things I have to go back and forth to see both views. I’d rather be able to scroll up and down to see the next day just like I can when I’m in upcoming. 

- I’d like reminders to repeat until I mark something complete. If I fail to complete something one day, remind me the next day at the same time. 

- finally I wish the things would show up on my lock screen if they are marked important or past a deadline or something. I previously used the iOS reminder app and I liked that my outstanding todos stood on my lock screen as a constant reminder. I’m not sure if this is possible but worth asking :)

Overall I feel like I have toooo much to do lately and Things is helping a lot. These additions would make it help even more!

author: T Larson

title: Disappointing: the first 1 star review I have ever given
body:
I depend heavily on to do lists for my job, I previously have used the free versions of Wunderlist and Todoist to stay organized. Ultimately, I was very happy with Todoist but upon going into the App Store to update it, I stumbled upon things 3. I was intrigued by the positive reviews and design awards and saw this as an opportunity to improve my productivity (I really liked the fact that it could sync with your calendar and that you could add notes to an event). However, these two added benefits do not compensate for the lack of overall usability and functionality. 

A few of my complaints:
-it is insanely challenging to schedule reoccurring events. With Wunderlist and Todoist I could just type “send monthly reports on the second Tuesday of every month” and it would automatically schedule it, or I could say “do blah blah tomorrow” and it would schedule it. This was the nicest feature that I would think a 50 dollar app would have
-you can’t create due dates for subtasks. A lot of times I have a project that is due one day, but I have predecessors that must be completed on days prior, there is no way to arrange this in things (once again, a feature that free competing tools offer)
-you can’t check off reoccurring events!!! This drives me nuts as it seems like such a simple feature. I schedule a reoccurring event and make it due a certain day, and although it shows up on that day, you can’t check it off so I don’t know if I’ve done it yet. And if I don’t complete it, it just goes away the next day so
I don’t remember to do it. 

These are just a few of many usability complaints I have. However, I am happy to change my review pending the experience provided by the app is improved

title: Awesome
body:
I have been searching and waiting for years for an app to come along that would finally allow a workflow that encompasses both the simple day-to-day tasks as well as complex projects. Things 3 is the best solution I have found so far. After a month of using it I have purchased and installed it for the iPhone, iPad, and Mac. I open it and work with it dozens of times a day.

Of course, the app is excellent for simple “To do” lists and works beautifully in a GTD workflow. The Tags functionality is very helpful with that.

As a surgeon who owns and runs my practice as a small business owner, as a husband and father, as someone who enjoys traveling, and as one who volunteers in various church and community organizations, I want to thank the Things 3 team for getting this app so right! I feel so much more in control of all areas of my life because Things 3 helps me to get everythig organized — and I can even save the lists I’ve come up with and reuse them for a similar task later!

The Areas feature is super helpful. I love being able to create projects and nest headlines into them. Task lists and even nested checklists within checklists for complex procedures — including parts to purchase, steps to take beforehand, and procedures that require several appointments to complete — all can be entered into Things, saved as templates, and customized for each patient. Brilliant!

I plan to be a lifelong user and hope the Things team will keep this product alive and improving for decades to come!

title: Wish there were pop-up alerts
body:
Pretty good app - I'm looking for a better solution than Reminders for iPhone, as the Reminders app is buggy and sketchy performance. This app, Things, is neat and well-arranged, with nice checkboxes to clear items from your to-do list, etc. which I appreciate. However, you have to go into the app to see what's next, with no alert pop-up anywhere that I can find. I need tasks to pop up and remind me to do this or that, sometimes at a specific time, and often more than once. Like a bill I need to pay, which I may remind myself a week before but need to wait to pay it until a few days later, so I need to have a second reminder so I don't forget.

Bills are just one example (still haven't found a good bill-pay app, either) - it could be a purchase I need to make but now I won't have time today after work, so I have to postpone until tomorrow after work. Or it may be a phone call I have to make at a specific time.

Overall, very good for keeping track of tasks, as long as you remember to look at it.

body: The ease and usefulness of this app helps very much in my busy schedule. I work in the film industry and projects come flying at you in all different directions and this has simplified my life drastically. Great for bad organizers and good for great ones.
author: tfrancois8

title: Easy to use and robust
body:
Impressive user experience design! Use is intuitive and the number of taps to perform an action seems fewer than the other more expensive apps I tried. You can pretty much figure out how to use it on your own, but they include a very nice tutorial in the form of a project with a list of to do’s. Very easy way to get up and running fast. 

It has all the features that I was looking for except for location alerts. My workaround is to create a tag for my locations and just search that tag. It would be nice to get a push notification. OTOH, it seemed like having that on for an app that I tried may have been sucking battery. I’m not sure. 

One slick feature is that repeating to dos have a lot of flexibility. You can even schedule them to repeat based on when you complete the task. So instead of repeating every 7 weeks, for example, the next one comes due 7 weeks after you completed the previous one. Nice.

title: Just started and already in love

The fact that it goes beyond a good system to make it a joy to use is why it earns five stars though. 

Things 3 is simple, intuitive, beautiful. Invest in it and invest in yourself.

title: Great!

title: Love this app

author: things jimbo

title: Things 3 Attains a Kind of Perfection
body: First two versions were good but Things 3 synthesizes all the lessons from previous iterations and gets as close to perfect as I’ve seen in a list-based management tool. Integration with calendars, Siri, and reminders is terrific, and the ability to add structure from groups of projects, to the project level, to task areas, to lists of to dos, and then bullets and notes within each granular level task reflects the reality of complex projects.  It’s also beautiful.  Five stars.

title: Peace of Mind
body: This is a great app. It is self explanatory. You can brain dump everything you know you have to do. You can categorize all of your tasks and projects, set their level of urgency. title: Too bright needs dark mode
body: The app is good, but the user interface is too bright. It needs a dark mode badly.
author: jATLhokie

title: Nice todo/checklist app
body:
This is a pretty basic todo or checklist style app that does what it does really well.  It got an Apple design award I suspect for its slick interface and uses Apple’s latest and greatest features like drag and drop which is helpful in doing things in less steps and makes using the app more intuitive.  But it’s not that powerful.  So, it’s a bit more form over substance. 

It’s not really a task manager like Omnifocus that can handle custom views and lots of nested and sub tasks, etc.  Omnifocus is a bit more substance over form. 

So, I use Omnifocus for work to manage hundreds of pending projects and tasks and Things 3 for my personal small checklists.

title: Just about perfect
body: This app is exactly what you want from a task Managment tool.   Well designed and the more I’ve used it the more nice touches I find. Well done!   Otherwise would love direct syncing to Alexa lists as well but just a fantastic product.
author: gsquared007

title: Wonderful app!
body:
I got Things 3 to help keep myself organized while finishing University. It is a wonderful app and very aesthetically pleasing! Well done! I am very pleased with this app! It has been easy to learn and use! Thank you!

My suggestions after a few weeks with it:
Have some integration with the Calendar app or Fantastical to generate to-do’s when you create an event in the calendar and vice-versa. Also with subscribed calendar feeds. My school automatically generated a calendar feed for us to subscribe to that shows assignment due dates. That would be awesome if Things would generate to-do’s and due dates based on that. Basically, the more integration with Calendar or Fantastical, the better!

author: Peter from MV

title: UI, GTD and Features
body:
First of all This app is great and definitely worth the money you paying.
For GTD users:
I can assure you that there is no app that can help you to implement full GTD in your life like Things! It is simple, ubiquitous, action oriented and a good planner.
About features:
There are some missing features that can improve this app way more.
- text recognition for tags, projects and due dates. when I type my to-do it will be greatly for me to just add my tags, choose between my projects and set a due date just by typing some symbols like # or @

- attach files from Dropbox, iCloud and etc. There is no need to attach files directly into Things, but it’ll be helpful if I could go to files or folders I need right from Things.

author: astromezzo

title: Changed My Relationship to the Word “Responsibility”
body:
It’s the weirdest feeling, but I actually LIKE responsibilities now! With Things I tell myself “I GET to do this...” even if it’s not all that interesting.

There’s something about the way it’s designed that makes it truly remarkable for the user.

This company clearly takes pride in what they do. This app is by far the most inspiring tool I’ve ever used.

Life can be challenging, but Things makes it infinitely more fun and engaging. I feel like I’m playing a video game while using it.

I’ve had so many disparate ways of managing my responsibilities, and to think that I could actually find an app to use on my phone to sync my priorities into one place seemed like a bad idea since I already spend so much time on it.

But the time I spend on Things is easily the best use of my time throughout the day, and I’m always thinking of how to use it more intelligently.

I am so grateful for this app and I really hope to use it for the rest of my life. Seriously. Keep it up guys!!!

title: Over Hyped
body: For what this app does, I really think it’s over priced and over hyped. It has some nice features like I can see my today list on my apple watch. It does what it says but its not really more than a simple list todo app. I really wish there was a calendar view. Like in ‘Upcoming’, if you could tap the calendar icon and actually see a calendar. There’s no way to see details more than a week in advance. So if you like to plan out your month, this isn’t the app for you. Also, when I am scheduling a repeating task on a specific day for the next week, the app doesn’t recognize the day. It always wants to repeat on Wednesday and I have to change it. Its minor, yes, but still annoying. Same thing with repeating a monthly task. It doesn’t recognize the date and I have to manually put it in. Honestly, I regret buying it. There are cheaper and better options on the app store.

title: Almost Perfect
body:

As a former lover of Wunderlist, this is the only app that I’ve found to meet (and maybe exceed) that service.

- an option for a subscription. I would love to pay you on a reoccurring scheduling for access to all your apps, rather than paying for each app individually.
- basic collaborative lists (shared, and assigned tasks)
- able to check off reoccurring tasks early
- address some infrequent flicking of the interface when moving between task lists (iPhone X)

title: Back to Things
body:
When I first left the world of paper only task and calendar management (former Day-Timer and then Franklin Covey user for 20+ years), I kept searching for the “time management holy grail” that would replace my paper planner. I started with Things and then Things
2.0 but kept hearing that it wasn’t being supported (unfounded rumors). I wandered to other programs such as Todoist (not a fan of karma), Wunderlist, etc.

Then, I saw a video of Things 3. Elegant design, intuitive features, the ability to put notes right on the task or the project caught my attention and imagination again. The ability to shape the interface of projects to my areas of responsibility was a real plus. I think in roles and responsibilities and to access projects that way is a real bonus. 

The synch is almost immediate and very reliable. Kudos to the creators who went underground and hammered out an elegant piece of software that is now, coupled with iCal and Evernote, my big three! 

Note: if you could add photos, files and pdf.s to it, this would be amazing!

title: Great job, but not enough to get me from from OmniFocus
body:
Things 3 is one of the best-designed apps I’ve yet used. It’s simple, pretty, and offers some real moments of delight.

One of my favorite design choices is the ability to assign a task to a day that is distinct from its due date—it may be due Friday, but I intend to do it Wednesday. (the closest OmniFocus offers is “defer until”, but deferring is a different intent, really.)

I have tons of tasks and projects already in OmniFocus, and there is an AppleScript-based importer which made carrying the data over possible (obviously requires the Mac client). The tasks and projects seemed, upon basic review, to have come across in good shape, which was also lovely.

Two matters ultimately prevented my switching over, however:

1. There should be a button to create a task in the widget, like OmniFocus’s has. I use this mechanism all the time in meetings. At the time of writing, its widget shows such a button only when it’s empty of tasks. This one is, at least, simple enough to solve.

2. I was hoping for advanced searching and saved searches. Things 3’s model of freely tagging tasks was what initially drew me; it promised to offer a bit of a relief from OmniFocus’s single-context assignment for its tasks… but that promise is only realized when a user could one day search an intersection of tags (and possibly omit others).

So, Things 3 is nice enough, but just short of able to pull me over from OmniFocus (i.e. compelling me to buy the Mac client after the demo period expired), given my financial and habitual investment in OmniFocus.

If I were coming to Things 3 from nothing, however, it’d be a lot harder a decision.

Great work, Cultured Code!

title: This is a premium app. Where are the premium functions?
body:

Where is the geofencing? Where is the reoccurring reminders? Where is sharing? Where is Alexa support? Why can’t I designate that when I open the app, it opens on a certain list? If I can’t decline the auto import of a task from another app, why even make me approve it? Am I supposed to be bowled over by exclusively by the UI of sparsity? I switched from Wunderlist to proactively prepare for when Microsoft nixes it completely, and I miss that near perfect product that was offered for free. Whereas with Things, I keep hoping that I’ve paid for a product that will get more feature rich, and I’m not seeing it.

title: Needs UX improvements
body:
UPDATE: they have a share extension thing so that’s good. But the other things still haven’t been addressed. 

The new Things is visually beautiful, but needs a few UX improvements:

- Show more than just one line of text per item. I shouldn’t have to tap into a task to read the whole thing. “Write shorter tasks” isn’t a good answer. 

- Show tasks that have a due date ABOVE those that don’t. The “someday” categorization to our those at the end of a project list requires additional taps. If I’ve given something a date, it’s MORE important than things that don’t have dates. 

- The app needs a share extension so that you can add items from other apps. (Update: they have one of these.)

title: Things is an ecosystem

title: Decent, but it can easily be better
body:
1. Keep the tags icon shown. Don't hide it when there's already tags on an item. Things changes the work flow when you go through many tasks. At least add the options to keep it shown in settings.

2. Swipe right needs to have more edit features. When you're editing an individual task, there's the "Move, Delete, More" menu down at the bottom. Add all the features of a task to that. As in, add "When", "Tags", "Deadline", "Move", etc - put ALL of them there. Then, when you swipe right to select many task, instead of having the "When, Move, Delete" menu at the bottom, just use the same menu as the individual task menu. This just adds consistency and allows us to edit more tasks quicker. Especially if I have a few tasks with the same deadline, I have to edit each individual task indepently and that takes forever.

3. Bring the keyboard hide button down with the keyboard. Or at least be able to drag it to the four corners of our content. This is really irritating with the plus models since I have to move my hands all over my phone just to put the keyboard away with the button.

4. Create a product key system so people can download the app for free, mess around with the demo project (just disable them to add anything other than what is described by the Project). Then, when they want to officially use the app, existing users can enter in their product key for a discounted upgrade price, and new users can purchase their product key for full price. This will allow people who are unfamiliar with the app to try it out, encourage existing users to stay, and maintain the $10 entry price. Obviously this system will have to keep track of which ipad/iphone/mac version of the app the user has purchased (to ensure the user pays the correct entry price), but that's three easy flags to keep track of.

title: Almost perfect
body:
Things 3 is a great looking app that does exactly what you need, but no more. You can see that the team which was building the app, had a lot of experience with To Do apps, but for some things and functionalities  they are stuck in 2008.

Advantages of the Things 3:

Great design (they won an Apple award for it)
Easy of use and intuitiveness 
Enough of complexity that it can cover most of your tasks and workflows. Things 3 will cover 99% of most users need, in a most elegant fashion.

Also it is not that expensive so I can understand that some functionalities are off the menu, but some things should definitely be included for the price that they ask.

Disadvantages of Things 3 (which should be included for a price).

No API!?!? Hello it’s 2017, we have a lot of tasks and software and devices, we need ability to create tasks from other sources, like emails handlers, 3rd party apps, IFTTT…. Pure sloppiness (or laziness), I expected more from Cultured Code.
No Web version. Ok, I get it, it’s difficult to develop for a whole new eco-system, but at least to have some basic web interface which we can create a basic To Do, and edit it later from Mac or iPhone. Again, pure sloppiness. A Web app would be  preferred. (told you they are stuck in 2008)
Not being able to create a task from a calendar event in the Upcoming view.
No official tutorial document. There is a support page where you can get most of the info you need, but for the price an official user guide would be great. A lot of excellent tips on how to use some things on their Twitter account, but not on their website. 

Understandable disadvantages (which are understandable considering the low price).

No Win or Android apps. They are focused on the Apple eco-system, covering all platforms is expensive development (still web version should be included for the price)
No file attachments. I understand this, storage is expensive.
Not account managed (except the iCloud sync), and since it’s not account managed…
No collaboration. No accounts no collaboration. 

Things 3 is an excellent app, which I use day to day, but it lacks “this much” to be perfect! 4 out of 5!

Cultured Code, go and build us a web version. Or an API. Much love.

title: Sharing why Things3 won't get any more money from me
body:
We all like pretty apps and Things3 is definitely that.  But form follows function, right?  Lots of reviews gush over the aesthetics of Things3, granting a pass for its shortcomings.  I do not.

I currently use Wunderlist, which is free and excellent but is going away and is not as pretty as Things3 (though certainly not ugly).  So I purchased Things3 for iPhone because of all the gushing positivity.  I held back on purchasing the iPad version and the MacOS version until I knew if Things3 had legs.

My biggest issues: 
1. Having to buy the app separately for iPad, iPhone and Mac.  I'm OK with buying apps separately for iOS and MacOS but you are pushing me too far by charging for iPad and iPhone.  I won't participate in supporting that unsavory business decision.  This is particularly unpalatable considering the relative awesomeness offered for free by Wunderlist.  This fact will be the one to send me off to seek further for a comprehensive, non-money-gouging, alternative.  And that's a shame, because Things3 has a lot of potential.  I'm happy to pay for quality apps but I won't pay  an unfair price.  It's a loss of a sale for the Things3 folks.  Because I refuse to be gouged twice on the iOS platform I won't be buying the MacOS version of Things3.  Give that some thought.

2. No shared tasks.  Example: My wife and I use Wunderlist with a shared/synchronized grocery list to which we each add things.  Whichever of us goes to the store, we share a common list.  Nothing like that for Things3.  End result: my wife has not purchased Things3 for her phone.  We still use Wunderlist for that feature.  It's another loss of a sale for Things3 folks.  My wife's phone remains free of Things3.

3.  No file attachment support, for images in particular.  Wunderlist allows me to add a photo (or other file) to my tasks.  This can be very useful.  Heading to the store for a replacement nut and bolt?  Take a pic of the old one and attach it to your task.  Wunderlist allows this, Things3 does not.  Sure I could swipe through my photos app, leaving it cluttered with otherwise unimportant photos but I'd rather have the photo of the bolt in my to do list, right there with the To-do.  

I invite the Things3 folks to consider the consequences to their revenue stream, particularly as it relates to items 1 & 2 above.  Make some changes and I'll buy your app for my wife and a copy for each of our Macs, too.  But until then, no more money from me.

title: 5 Stars for UI—but missing too many features
body:
The UI is beautiful. To be honest, for a lot of people that use OmniFocus or 2Do, this is the lure that will draw you in to spend the extra dollars. It looks good, and OmniFocus hasn't updated their UI for a while and 2 Do can seem really clunky... so you download this app only to realize that it's mainly all looks. 

If you have a to-do for example that says, "Call Mom" there is no contact integration to make the call from inside the app like there is on 2Do. How amazingly awesome would that be? 

There's not any email integration—because there's no contact integration... would love to set a to-do to email someone and I could go right into emailing them to complete the to-do. 

If you have multiple tasks to add and would like to rapid fire them all while you have it fresh, there's no way to continue to quickly add tasks. This is where 2Do and OmniFocus thrive... missing Quick Add, or Save+ so that you don't have to save the app tap the "magic circle" then tap the title... make it faster. 

The native Reminders app that comes stock on iPhone has location-based reminders. The other top apps have location-based reminders. Things 3 doesn't. 

No sharing options.

Things 3 doesn't really play nice with other apps. No API's available which means it doesn't integrate with other apps. 

I like the ability OmniFocus for Mac has to highlight anything anywhere and just use a Mac keyboard shortcut to add it into OmniFocus. This is much needed on Things 3. 

Also missing the ability to send your email into Things 3 to add a to-do. 

There's a few other minor things that I believe would make this so much better, but there's a reason why I have continuously downloaded Things 1, Things 2, and now Things 3 and then have fallen in love with the UI, but keep leaving it behind almost immediately. 

If you like some more features than the stock Reminders app—like having lists inside of lists inside of lists, yet don't mind losing some features from the stock reminders app—like location-based reminders, sharing lists, integrating with a lot of other apps, then perhaps Things 3 is for you. 

If you like bare simplicity, this app may also be for you. 

But if you're looking for something that does a lot more than the stock Reminders app your iPhone already comes with, I'd recommend 2Do or OmniFocus. They are tried and true and their reviews speak for themselves. 

If you have extra money and want to spend it on trying this app out... I'd wait until Things 3 comes out with some more basic yet useful features now that we are in 2017.

title: Just what I was looking for
body:
A while back, I did an extensive search for a task manager to fit my workflow. Nothing felt quite right, so I stuck with Wunderlist. Things 3 was what I was waiting for without knowing it! I read lots of reviews, took the Mac app for a free spin, and even seriously reconsidered Todoist before making a decision. The simplicity, beauty, and core features of Things 3 won me over. Sure it has some limitations (no online version, no shared lists, etc.), but it's brilliant in its strengths. And it's just delightful to use! Todoist has more features, but it's a real bore. 

Here are a few features I love about Things. (1) It looks and "feels" fantastic. There are lots of great online reviews that rave about this, and they're right! The user experience makes me want to use this every day (and that's a good thing for a daily task manager). (2) It has an outstanding Mac app. (3) It syncs with native Apple Calendar so you can see your calendar events in Things! (4) It syncs with Apple Reminders in such a way that you can add to Things using Siri! (5) The tag system is great and filtering by multiple tags is super easy. You can filter by any tags in all views, including "Today." (6) You can postpone tasks till "This Evening" within the "Today" view. (7) It's a one-time payment, not a subscription. 

I could go on and on. Things won't be for everyone, but it was just what I was looking for. Well worth the investment (on iOS and Mac) for a program that keeps me focused and organized every single day.

title: The only to-do app that STICKS. Worth every cent.
body:
Apple's Reminders is just the ugliest, most horrendously un-useful junk on the planet. Reminders doesn't "stick" with me, largely due to the terribly cumbersome and ornery interface. In Reminders, the only way you can set a reminder for today is to tie it to an exact time, and then it just still isn't prevalent enough. Reminders is the whiny dweeb you just sigh at and want to get away from.

Enter Things. It sticks. It's simple. No instruction manual needed. Advanced functions just take a tiny bit of trial and error. But the best part about Things is its Inbox concept, which is a catch-all for your tasks. Then, only if you want to, you can swipe left on the to-do and set it to Today or a specific date. Not only is this app terrific for organizing your day, you can organize your entire week and month whenever tasks get invariably pushed back.

Buy Things. It's worth every last penny. The Mac version is too expensive, but it's there if you need it. This is the to-do app you've been searching for. I remember attending the WWDC where this app was recognized by its small developer team for an Apple Design Award. I don't know why on Earth Apple just did not acquire the team of awesome designers and engineers who create it.

Second, add Today items into the Upcoming view. By that, I mean I'd like to have an option to focus on just Today but also to focus on today and what's upcoming. title: Perfect for my non collaborative tasks and projects
body: For years I have struggled to find a good software program to manage all of my task and project management needs. For the last several of those years I have used Asana almost exclusively. But I have come to realize is that it was too much software for most of my needs. While I do need Asana or some similar application for collaborative work, I simply do not need that much horsepower for managing most of the activities of my life, personal and professional. Things is the very best I have found for these vast portions of my busy life that do not involve collaboration. I have yet to find a feature that I need that is not in this software. title: Expensive
body:
This app works great & it works for what I need it to do. 
The fact that you have to pay full price for each new update really takes me out of the game, let alone the fact that although you can share lists across devices you have to pay full price for each device you use it on. 

There is no bundle, no slightly discounted price for buying more than one platform only $50 for mac, $10 for iPhone & $20 for the iPad version. It's just not worth it. 

There is no loyalty discount nothing of the sorts. 
If you ask about it you get the same standard answer that is written multiple times everywhere "things 3 are completely different apps" therefore you need to pay full price for each. 

It is a shame, I've already purchased other similar apps and I should not have paid the $10 for a new one. Hopefully enough people will be silly enough to keep paying the $80 to get it across all platforms in order for them to stay in business. As for me, I will be going elsewhere from now on.

title: Intuitive, gorgeous, exactly what I needed
body:
Before trying this app I'd been using a combination of places to keep track of my work to-do's, grocery list, mental notes... they were all over the place. I was never able to remember what I needed to do when I needed to do it. Each morning I was overwhelmed just trying to figure out what exactly I should be accomplishing that day. 

Enter Things! I bought it on my iPad first, and after entering everything into the inbox and then sorting into projects and categories, I instantly felt better. This app is intuitive, it's beautiful, and it makes me want to open it every day unlike any other management tools I've used (google keep, trello, clear, notes, my sketchbook) It's my one trusted place to keep and organize everything I need to do. 

My favorite part is the "today" section where I can see my upcoming meetings and things I need to do that day and that evening. Do yourself a favor if you're new to this, like I was, and read "Getting things done" — this app works AMAZINGLY well for that system. 

Thanks for designing and building such a life changing product!

title: Things 3 is a Joy
body:
Simple yet powerful. Clean an organized. Three things made me switch: Siri integration, lists within tasks, and projects with headings. 

I love the integration with Siri and the Reminders app. All I do is say “Siri, remind me to …” and the elusive task is immediately captured, waiting for me in the Things 3 Inbox. Genius! 

I really like the “lists” you can create inside a task. It reduces the number of “tasks” and results in an uncluttered look. A bonus is the ability to convert a task with lists into a Project with Tasks. Again, genius. 

I like the Projects feature and the ability to have Headings within. As I mentioned, simple yet powerful. 

Quality program, nicely done on the Mac and iPhone. I can’t wait to try Things 3 when I get my new iPad Pro!

title: Useless reminder notifications
body:
Three stars for a beautiful, intuitive app that is fantastic for quickly adding tasks to your to do list. 
I was looking to this app to replace both Apple's pre-installed Reminders app and Todoist, which is far too expensive for a list app. 
I love using Things, however the one issue that makes this not so great is the way notifications work when you set up a reminder for a specific task. The reminder will go off and show on your lock screen, but as soon as you unlock your phone the reminder is gone. And then you forget about it! I would really love the option for it to stick to the screen instead of disappearing from existence. It does the opposite of reminding me to do something!

Besides that, the interface is lovely and I highly recommend the app, especially if the above Notifications gripe doesn't bother you.

title: I surrender
body:
It was a long, painful wait for this update. I'd given up on Things a long time ago, bouncing around from one to-do app to another. I told myself that the delay was too long and that I'd never commit myself to this vaporware.

Then Things 3 arrived and I tried it. And since that moment, I have used it more consistently and with more satisfaction than any other productivity app I've ever tried. That includes OmniFocus, 2Do, Remember The Milk, The Hit List, Appigo To Do, Todoist, Midnight Inbox, Wunderlist, TaskPaper, Clear, and Apple's own Reminders app (even with GoodTask or Fantastical as the UI).

Some of those apps actually were a good fit for me, but they disappeared or never delivered after a long development effort. Others were good, but required too many changes to my long-baked-in habits.

Task entry, organization, and scheduling are all easy. It's as sophisticated as I need it to be, while also being quick and easy and not requiring that I spend more time managing tasks than I do completing them. Things 3 feels natural and easy. Is it the answer for everyone? Of course not. Is it the the one for me? Yes.

title: This is the To Do app I've been waiting for
body:
I've purchased so many iPhone to-do apps. I've never been happy with any of them. I use them for a while, but I never feel fully settled with them, and so then I start relying more on paper and my brain. Eventually the app ceases to be my main repository and things get just as muddled as ever. However, there is something special about this app. It's designed just right, and so I actually use it, and the more I use it, the more reliable it becomes, and the more reliable it becomes, the more I use it. Finally, I feel comfortable putting the clutter from my brain elsewhere. I haven't yet completely abandoned paper lists, but, for the first time, I feel like that's a possibility. 

It's hard to say exactly what makes this so much better than all the other to-do apps. For me, it feels like the difference between the UI of iOS vs Android. They both have their adherents, but one feels natural and intuitive to me, and one feels clunky and confusing. I'm not exactly sure why. The only other to-do app I've ever used that had that special feel for me was an old Palm app by Llamagraphics called Life Balance, but the creator suffered a brain injury so that one sadly never fully made the transition to iOS. 

Comparing apples to apples, there's one thing that makes this absolutely superior to Things 2 - the checklist within a checklist. I use that feature all the time.

title: I'm unsatisfied.
body:
I don't enjoy the gestures- it's not intuitive to hide basic function. I'd rather be presented with options as I create an event than them being hidden. The setup of the lost areas is weird, still adjusting.  In the name of simplicity I find the overall interface confusing. 

I also find the lack of a few features disappointing. Where are the location based reminders? Why do I have to keep clicking different menus to add a specific event time? I need reminded. That's the whole point of buying this. It should be easy and obvious. 

If this had a trial, I probably wouldn't have bought it.  The integration of the apple default to do list was a big +1 for me, but I can't just use Siri as it says. You use Siri, she ads it to your default list app. Then later you have to hit a button in the tasks app that imports the task. Just auto import!!! 

Why is deleting a task not one of the quick swipe options? This is something you find in most other apps, such as email, so please understand there is a reason to follow convention. 

Overall, I bought this because I wanted to avoid a subscription to some of the alternative organizational apps. However, at the moment, I find myself disappointed and wishing I would have just ponied up a few extra dollars. 

Edit: the apple watch implementation is spot on and may really save this app for me. Again, I still want this to be more active notification wise, but I really like it on Apple watch now that I've set it as a complication.

title: Beautiful With Limitations
body:
PROS: As others have mentioned this is a beautiful piece of software. Clean modern look with a balance of simplicity and functionality. There are 4 levels of hierarchy- Areas, Projects, To-dos, and Checklists. There's also the ability to have text headings to help further group the last three levels. Easy to move around and rearrange. Integrates your calendars into Today view, which is very nice.

CONS: Projects and To-dos can have start dates, but only Projects can have deadlines.  Checklist items can't have dates at all. 

Text only input. No photos can be attached. URLs can be pasted as text, but are not clickable.

Areas can't be collapsed. So if you have, say, Work, Home, Financial, and Family Areas, each with a dozen Projects, you end up scrolling down and down through each Area and all their Projects to get to your last Area. 

To-dos can be converted to Projects, but you can't convert Projects to To-dos.

Found no internal way to back up your data.

OVERALL: Beautiful, but missing a few things I need.

title: Better than "Reminders", but not a replacement
body:
I love this app. I was skeptical at first but after fully committing it's been a great way to create better project management/routine management than Notes and Reminders, but without the sketch pad nature of Microsoft OneNote. Creating "projects" and then organizing to-do's within them, broken down by "headers", allows a way more simplified, clutterfree look st your to-do list, but also allowing you to easily include notes about the to-do that are easily accessible (combining reminders and notes best aspects). 

This app is not for daily, hour sensitive reminders. At the beginning of the day, all the stuff that is due at the end of the day (or should be started by the day) generate a notification. So if you need to take your medication at 4 pm, you'll get a notification/to-do in your list when you wake up, which is annoying because then you'll have a to-do all day until 4. For that reason, I now use Reminders jointly with Things, but still use Things more. 

One minor annoyance (if you have used Reminders/Outlook a lot) is the repeatable tasks section does not have a good UI, and takes a bit to wrap your head around CultureCode's logic. Ex: I need something repeating on 25th of month, so I need to set date to next 25th, but also say that it will repeat on the 25th of every following month. If you fail to do both properly, you will cause it to generate a reminder on the following but not current month at one of the days. Then there's the create deadline for repeating reminders, which actually sets the deadline for the day you set above, and then starts a reminder X number of days before. 

I'm giving this 5 stars because I appreciate it primarily for keeping my blog projects in order very neatly, and other long term projects for work/life separate and trackable. Users of Omnifocus will probably find this a bit too simplified, and lacking the depth of a computer science/engineer-designed task/project manager. This will probably work well if you are not in CS, and don't use Outlook religiously (for both work/life).

title: Perfect for a Wunderlist Convert
body:
Since the demise of Wunderlist is imminent, I needed a replacement that would fill all of my task management needs. Things 3 is exactly what I needed. I was very happy with the way Wunderlist was organized, but I was surprised how much simpler Things 3 was in several respects:

1) I love the ability to put deadlines on items and setting how many days in advance it should start to show in my today list. This was a glaring omission in Wunderlist, where I'd have to switch back and forth between the today and week view in order to see upcoming tasks that require several days of attention. 

2) Most of my tasks come in via email from various customers everything day. I need to capture those requests quickly and easily reference notes in the email when I start working on the task. I used the mail to Wunderlist feature to automatically add tasks that came in via email. It worked great until Microsoft bought Wunderlist and then it started becoming unreliable. Things 3's uses shortcuts on Mac and 'share' on iOS to automatically add tasks for incoming email that includes a link to pull up the email in the mail client. I actually prefer this to embedding the content directly in the task as Wunderlist did. 

3) Adding reminders using Siri is finally useful as the tasks can be automatically imported in to Things!

4) The Apple Watch app actually works to check things off the list. Wunderlist had a terrible interface that requires you to hit a tiny checkbox directly center. It would take 10 tries before it would check off and then a while before it synced back up with the app.

All in all I'm super pleased with the app and recommend the Mac, iPhone, and iPad versions. They are pretty expensive, but worth it if you handle a deluge of tasks each week.

Pros
It now allows you to set alarms; you can now change a task into a project; you can now have sub-tasks within your tasks; it has a neat separator that you can use within projects for yet another level of organization; the sync between iterations of the app on your devices is solid and quick

Cons

The aesthetics make it a joy to use and the drawbacks aren't a deal killer for me (maybe for those that must have collaborative options).

My office.  Complete w printer.  I don't have time to be Opening up laptop every time I need to reset and find my next priority or audible I need to call to stay most efficient.  The point of a to do app is to mow through as much data, SELF-DRIVEN data as possible, but a small screen like that is a highly unnatural state to view information, the iPhone is the single most adaptable invention ever, for people you'll never meet and can't imagine, we are all different, I was hoping for good things with this app, that's why I bought it, and I won't ask for a refund because maybe there will be some development w phone or product, and I cannot say a bad thing about this app, it is brilliant and beautiful and calming even which best indicates its quality, but unless it flips sideways I won't be using it any time soon. There are some nice small additions and a wonderful interface but that is about it.
The biggest issue with this software is the lack of real integration with Apple Reminders and Calendar. You essentially have to use one app or the other as far as Apple Reminders go. As for Calendar, it's nice seeing entries within Things 3, but you can't edit or interact with these. If the app were able to synch back and forth with Reminders and Calendar, I might use Things 3. 

This app is basically just a fancy task list with a very pretty interface...For 80$.

title: It's a Things Thing! V.3 Brings Me Back From Todoist
body: I'm glad to be back with Things v3 on my iPhone 7-Plus and on my iPad 2. I have not yet purchased the Mac OS license for my Mac Book Pro and my iMac. There is much to like in v3. Syncing between the two iOS devices is flawless and seems instantaneous. The layout and user interface is clean and easy. I like the "areas of focus" as well as "projects" and even checklists inside tasks. Lots of versatility there. I also like the flexibility of tags. Nitpicks: I don't  like the visual typography subjugation of projects to focus areas. I think they should be represented more equally as a typography matter. I'd also like more options to create projects and lists right from an add-task dialogue. Also, I like incorporating the calendar, but I'd like more vigorous infusion of calendar functions. I'm glad to be back with Cultured Code. It's a Things thing.

title: Great app
body:
This is a highly functional and very beautifully designed to do app. It is easy and fun to create new inbox items, new projects, and new items to do today. It also has recurring events, and time-based alerts. You can set up Siri so that the app captures items added to Reminders. The watch app is pretty nice with the large modular complication allowing you to see three different events and it is delightful to check them off from the watch.

A few nagging things for me and include no location based alerts, and having to manually "import" items added to the inbox using Siri, so that I can't just use the watch to create items to do today that didn't show up on the watch without opening the phone app first.

For me personally, GTT never looked and worked better. 

I splurged and purchased all three versions (Mac, iPad, iPhone) to use the free sync between them. Even though it's refreshing to pay once to own it and get to use the free sync, I hope for the developer's sake that they haven't put themselves in a future pickle by opting to not charge any sort of ongoing subscription fee. 

Solid quality and solid buy recommendation.

title: Wow incredible!
body: I bounced around different todo apps a lot (Omnifocus, 2do, Todo, Wunderlist, Trello and even the previous version of Things) and had finally settled on combination of Omnifocus, Trello and just the plain old notes app for the times I got too lazy. Although my system worked relatively well, I always felt there had to be a better way: something less cumbersome than Omnifocus, more sophisticated and polished than Trello but still as easy to use as a notes app. This version of Things is incredible and has everything I could hope a todo app to have. The gestures and UX design are also pure genius: simple to use, but very powerful. I hadn't felt as excited about UX design as with this version of Things since the introduction of the iPhone. This is a game changer in the todo app space. The next step as I see it would be to allow collaborative working. I'm sure the Cultured Code team could figure out a way to make that beautiful and intuitive as well.

title: This changes everything!
body:
I am a longtime Things user [since the earliest days]. But I have also used most of the other GTD apps available for iOS and Mac. I keep returning to Things. We have been waiting for a very long time for this update. I am not disappointed.
At first, though, I did not like the GUI, preferring the color scheme of the originals. I felt it was a bit too cartoonish at first, but have really grown to appreciate it. Mind you, I am still quite fond of the old scheme, but can live with this one. 
I think the folks at Cultured Code have produced a game changer for everyone. I am more than happy to pay for all versions of this app, especially since they have not gone to a subscription model and since they have not charged for several years for their updates. I think it will be a long time before I go looking at any other GTD app.
Now, for the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly:
## The Good
Checklists. The ability to move tasks around within the iOS version. Reminder setting. Start dates and finish dates. The satisfying way a task is marked completed. Being able to subdivide project areas of focus. Setting things to be done in the evening. Having projects show up in the Sidebar under their area of focus. Did I mention checklists?
## The Bad
I do not like the way daily reviews are accomplished. The earlier versions highlights all tasks for the day and one could select individual tasks or easily select multiple tasks and quickly assign them to later dates. Not so with this version. I still like having a daily review, I just do not like the way it is accomplished. On the Mac, Quick Entry is not as smooth as in earlier versions. It takes a few more keystrokes to navigate through the task settings and sometimes I have to manually click into the window to change something. Everything should be easily navigable through the keyboard. On iOS, it sometimes is not readily evident how to assign a project to a task when creating a task.
## The Ugly
Though I an growing to like the GUI, I did prefer the old color scheme. Also, sometimes it takes forever for syncing to occur.

title: OK but still lacking import and collaboration features
body:
It's OK. 

Import features:
What it lacks and why I moved away last year were real import features. 
We live in a connected world and our tasks live on a bunch of other systems. (Trello, Jira, GitHub ...).
Manually entering these in Things just to have everything in one place is painful. 

Collaboration
There's no collaboration, at least at the very basic level available. The ability to set a task for someone, the ability to set a contact for a task has been deprecated. 
Come on guys. This should be addresed alreadyl.

Other issues:
1. Recurring task can't be saved in a project (only in an area) which defeats the purpose. 
2. Theres no way to see your recurring tasks if you're not saving them in an area (you have to search for them). This is a big oversight.
3. Areas are now behaving like projects but aren't projects. You can't have headings in them, but you can have anything else you have in a project. Decide what they are supposed to be and be consistent. Areas shouldn't be able to contain anything than projects or behave exactly like projects.

Yes, the app is nice, the micro-interactions are beautiful. I can see that a lot of thought went into this app, but guys, it's been years since the last major overhaul... years... I'm happy to pay up, I understand the work this took, as I'm a developer myself. Just move faster guys.

title: Finally, a task manager that just works
body:
Yes, I'm one of those people that has tried more task management apps then I care to admit. Some of them turned out to be cheap and simple but inadequate to my needs; others are more expensive and more powerful, but still have big gaps in functionality. 
Like other reviewers, I have been impressed with Things 3 clean, elegant interface. However, I have now moved from Omnifocus to Things not for beauty but primarily for one basic but (to me) critical difference: in Omnifocus, tasks are prone to disappear in between the "defer" date and the due date-- and manual kludges for such a basic feature should NOT be necessary in an expensive and otherwise powerful app. IMO that's a dealbreaker. 
Things 3, on the other hand, simply lets tasks to rollover in the Today view so you don't experience that nagging feeling that  something critical has disappeared from view. 

Things 3- it just works!

title: Good so far
body:
I've used 2Do for years. I think Things 3 has enough features to woo me away from 2Do. 

I like the streamlined nature of task entry and the Today / Upcoming / Anytime / Someday model. That said, I have plenty of feature requests. Some are just Nice to Haves, and some seem like mistaken omissions. Without further ado:

Things feature requests

	•	Would love dark mode
	•	Magic plus add button doesn't let me drag to today, someday, etc… Doesn't that seem like a fairly big omission?
	•	Way to batch add a tag to all selected items? Right now I can only move them all to a new project or area 
	•	Way to expand all tasks in an area and project so I can see everything - full task, notes, checklist etc. - without having to click
	•	Export mode that lets me email a project and have it look good in rich text - actual headings, check boxes etc - that is, other options for sharing format besides just markdown
	•	More important - when sharing an entire project via email/whatever, it doesn't share everything - need to share all checklists and notes too, not just task name
	•	Be able to drag a task into a project; right now I have to do it using the move menu
	•	Convert project back to task with checklist
	•	Way to assign different colors to different projects / areas so I can see at a glance how much I have to do in each area
	•	Map Siri reminder list to different projects. For example, if I say to Siri, add grapes to my shopping list, I would love for it to automatically go into the shopping list project in things.  It won't even appear in my things inbox if I don't put it in the main reminder list on Siri.
	•	Shake to undo; sometimes I accidentally change something on a task - like taking it out of today - and then I have to go find it. Shake to undo would simplify this.

title: My new GTD system
body:
With the new release of Things 3, I have switched my GTD system over to this suite of products (I bought iOS versions and Mac client). It was a pleasant surprise to find how useful it is to have your top three to-dos on one's watch face. The apps are beautifully designed while still remaining simple to use. Great job by the team! I could go on and on about the quality of these products, but you really owe it to yourself to try them out if you are a personal productivity nerd like me. 

My only criticism is that there is no "Waiting For" special folder to sit alongside the Today, Upcoming, Anytime, and Someday folders for delegated tasks or simply things one is waiting for. As an example, I would normally make a task to track the arrival of a refund in the mail. Tasks added to this Waiting For folder would be parked (and hidden from the Anytime list of next actions) until due date or scheduled date arrived.

In the meantime, I am using the Someday folder as a proxy for a Waiting For folder. It's behavior is exactly how a Waiting For folder should work (tasks remain hidden from my other lists). The only downside is that now my personal someday list is cluttered with Waiting For items. But, technically, one could rationalize this use of the Someday folder because if one is waiting for a delegated task without any start or due date, it's technically someday. :-)

For anyone interested, I created a project in Someday called "Waiting For", so this is where I park all of those tasks. This at least separates them from my personal someday list. 

Finally, I'm glad this product does not have a team collaboration feature as I do not want to be forced to sign others up just so I can delegate a task. I'm happy without a true external delegation function with the exception of a true Waiting For folder per above comments.

Fantastic product and kudos to the design and development team.

title: Incredible

I have been so plessantly surprised with the intuitive workflow and UI after years of using Omnifocus to GTD. I love how seamlessly everything is laid out – a ton of features for power users but not too many to bloat the software up. I truly hope this is a renewed commitment to the app, given that we had to wait 5 years for it to develop into what it is now. Software is only worth it when the team keeps its users in the loop. title: A Brand New Face On A Limited App
body:
After about a week working with Culture Code's Things 3, one fact tops the list: this application makes adding and moving tasks effortless. Things 3 sets a new standard for simplicity, efficiency, and innovation in an iOS and MacOS task manager. 

But, it is also a fact that Things (now in it's 3rd version) still offers such a narrow view of task and project management. Those folks that prefer a simple, fast, fun app to manage their personal tasks should look no further then Things 3. But, if you need projects and tasks to do more: save Dropbox or iCloud Drive links, Evernote links, images, videos - you are seriously hampered by what Cultured Code can do for you. 

For example, you can drag anything from your MacOS iCloud Drive to a MacOS Things 3 note but that link is useless on iPhone and iPad. On iOS, Things 3's Upcoming list shows calendar appointments as read-only items (no interaction is possible). On MacOS, Things 3 displays calendar appointments as seemingly active links that don’t work. On several occasions, clicking a link here freezes the application. 

So, it is clear that Cultured Code prefers their customers to travel down a very narrow and limited road to personal task management. There is no task or project sharing with partners or teams. And, this is fine; many people don’t need it. Omnifocus, a major competitor, has provided no collaborative tools since ‘day one’.  

Things 3 has provided, perhaps grudgingly, two functions that their customers have been clamoring for: timed alerts, and calendar intergration. The visual and functional representation of these two tools seem like mere appeasements rather then something strongly innovative. 

All in all, Cultured Code has done a solid job of putting a brand new face on an aging and quite limited application. For my money, a sleeper product such as Nozbe is a far deeper and far more innovative task management system.

title: Perfection
body:
I have tried all the todo apps you can think of, and Things has always been the best. As a user of Things 2 since 2014, I have been eagerly awaiting Things 3. It is everything I hoped for and more. It has all of the features that made v2 great, as well as some new ones that make it much better.

The main concept is still wonderful, the Today list. You pick the tasks you want to complete today, drag them in any order, and go about your day. It works great, always has and always will. The Scheduled list in Things 3 has become Upcoming, in which you can actually plan your days ahead for the next week as well as the future months and years. It works great, as in Things 2 you couldn’t set the specific order of what you wanted to do the next day. Similarly, the Next list has become Anytime, which also works well.

Projects have received a major overhaul that greatly increases productivity. The nice little progress indicator circles are a great addition, as well as the inclusion of Headings, to group your todos in any way you want inside a project.

Finally, the main aspect of Things 2 that I didn’t like was the lack of reminders, which is now included in Things 3! It works wonderfully. Additionally, more feature parity has been brought to the applications. For exampe, duplicating tasks and making existing tasks repeat were only possible on Mac; they are both now also possible on iOS

To conclude, this is a great app and I would recommend it to anybody.

The Magic Plus!

body:
I've been waiting years for an update. Was worth the wait. Just the right amount of power and sophistication while maintaining simplicity and an easy learning curve. It's a pleasure to use and it shows hat a lot of time and care went into this version. I do like that I pay once to own the App instead of paying a subscription. 

However, its not perfect. 
Doesn't support location based reminders. Doesn't allow repeating tasks to be within a project (for now). For some reason tasks cannot have a due date and be in the inbox simultaneously. This is by design, but I wish this were not the case. 

It would be nice to allow others to see and/or modify and/or join my todos online, but it's not a deal breaker for me.

Paying for a separate iPad version seems excessive since, according to the developers, all the versions share a lot of the same code. I'm fine paying for iOS and Mac separately, but the iPhone and iPad versions should just be one app.
